title: Calendar-specific fits retain a past SST radiation signal but leave its time direction uncertain in 1981-2013
abstract: We test whether seasonal immediate sensitivity explains a published past SST radiation signal. We use AMIP-minus-HighResMIP monthly differences in five model families. Each calendar month has its own immediate gain, cubic trend and sea-ice coefficient. For 1981-2013 the mean past coefficient is 0.656 [0.093, 1.191], while the future coefficient is -0.016 [-0.516, 0.496]. Their paired contrast is 0.672 [-0.155, 1.464]. Brackets give conditional 95% leverage-adjusted residual-block intervals. Thus the past association survives these seasonal controls, but total-radiation time direction remains unresolved over the full period. The all-sky-minus-clear-sky component supplies most of the point contrast. Later starts and volcanic exclusion give stronger contrasts. These exploratory fits do not identify a physical delay or a causal cloud response. Fixed predictors, experiment differences, shared model errors and limited records constrain inference. Code, exact input provenance, fit summaries, resampling draws and numerical checks are included.
